page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-192-metal is a bare-metal server configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at a base clock speed of 4.0 GHz, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning comprises 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance runs directly on bare metal without a hypervisor layer and does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core performance and parallel memory bandwidth. In stress-ng testing, multi-core throughput registered 160,623.56, placing it in the top tier alongside a PassMark CPU score of 123,975.15. Advanced instruction handling is reinforced by hardware acceleration features, including AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 (vnni and bf16), reflected in top-tier ratings for extended instructions (187,284.0) and encryption tests (164,812.22). Memory subsystems deliver 466.69 GB/sec read bandwidth and 202.24 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256MB blocks, paired with strong caching performance.

While aggregate computing capabilities rank in the upper decile, single-core benchmarks yield more moderate results. Single-threaded stress-ng throughput (2,017.09) and Geekbench single-core performance (2,133.0) place within average to strong brackets, and Geekbench text processing falls into lower percentiles (1,424.0). Storage reliance requires network-attached volumes because zero local block storage is included, which must be planned into deployment architectures requiring continuous high-IOPS disk persistence.

The qualitative hardware density offers high operational efficiency for parallel applications capable of saturating 192 threads and 768 GB of memory. It serves extensive in-memory databases, evidenced by 182.38 million Redis SET operations per second and high-throughput web processing (140.64 GB/sec). The profile is ideally targeted at large-scale parallel compilation, CPU-based LLM inference, intensive database operations, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-192-metal is a high-density bare-metal server driven by dual-socket Intel Xeon 8481C processors on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores) clocked at 4.0 GHz with 105 MB of L3 cache, complemented by 768 GB of DDR5 memory providing a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The platform contains no bundled GPUs and relies entirely on remote storage, as local disk is absent. Empirical testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by 160,623.56 in stress-ng and 123,975.15 in PassMark CPU, backed by AMX and AVX-512 vector acceleration. High-capacity memory bandwidth supports 466.69 GB/sec read speeds and up to 182.38 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread speeds remain in middle tiers, its immense parallel resource profile makes it well-suited for distributed container orchestration, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching platforms, and CPU-driven batch inference workloads.

768 GB high-speed DDR5 memory delivering up to 466.69 GB/sec read bandwidth
Integrated hardware acceleration including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8
